purpose: Distinguish evidence-gap qualifications from deliberate scope qualifications. Upgrade only claims for which stronger current evidence now supports the stated wording; preserve qualification where machine, mould, site, product-disposition or non-unique diagnostic boundaries are intrinsic to the claim.

newEvidence.title: Service plasticising — injection-unit configuration and plasticising components
newEvidence.scope: Machine-manufacturer guidance on screw/cylinder/non-return-valve components, dosage volume, residence/melting capacity, injection flow and pressure capability. Numeric recommendations remain ARBURG/application-specific and are not imported as universal Book setpoints.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow Insight — viscosity and flow simulation models
newEvidence.scope: Documents viscosity models dependent on measured material data, temperature, shear rate and pressure. Used for mechanism support, not as a production-material data source.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow Insight — designing the runner layout
newEvidence.scope: Documents sprue/runner/gate transport, runner pressure-drop effects, balance and dependence on material and processing conditions.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow Insight — Juncture Loss model
newEvidence.scope: Describes measured pressure loss through feed-system contractions such as sprue, runner and gate junctions and the influence of rheological quantities.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow — runner systems and gates
newEvidence.scope: Defines gates as the runner-to-cavity restriction and documents gate/runner geometry effects on pressure drop and filling.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow — Draft Angle result
newEvidence.scope: Documents shrink-on-core behaviour and the influence of draft, surface texture, part complexity, ejection depth and material on demoulding. Numeric examples remain context-specific and are not imported as universal Book rules.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow Insight — troubleshooting sink marks and voids
newEvidence.scope: Explains thermal contraction, thick-section effects and the surface-sink versus internal-void outcome when the outer skin resists deformation; also identifies packing/gate/cooling interactions.

newEvidence.title: Moldflow Insight — Injection Into Thin Section
newEvidence.scope: Documents early freeze, pressure-transmission loss and fill/packing consequences in thin sections. Used with machine-manufacturer thin-wall evidence; no universal thickness or speed threshold is adopted.

newEvidence.title: Ultramid T KR 4350 — Product Datasheet 2026
newEvidence.scope: Grade-specific storage/handling documentation requiring dry storage, careful resealing and condensation avoidance. Used only to corroborate that post-drying/post-opening handling can alter moisture condition; values are not generalized.

resolutions.reason: NIST experimental-design guidance supplies the controlled-comparison/statistical-method evidence that the original review identified as missing, while ISO anchors reproducible process description.

Machine-manufacturer and material-manufacturer evidence independently support screw plasticising/metering and the associated residence/thermal history, with exact implementation left machine/material specific.
Independent peer-reviewed and sensor-manufacturer evidence distinguishes local cavity-pressure measurement from upstream machine-side pressure after intervening flow-path losses.
A peer-reviewed switchover review and machine-manufacturer adaptive-control guidance directly support fill-to-hold control-objective change and process-dependent transfer/packing strategy.
Independent tooling/thermal/material evidence supports the interaction of cooling, contraction, geometry and release readiness. No universal cooling/ejection time is introduced.
Machine-manufacturer evidence now anchors the injection-unit screw/cylinder/non-return-valve hardware while material guidance independently corroborates the functional process context.
Direct in-mould temperature-monitoring guidance plus peer-reviewed cooling research supports that controller setpoint alone cannot establish uniform cavity-surface thermal condition.
Engineering rheology documentation directly models viscosity as condition-dependent on measured material data, temperature and shear rate; manufacturer guidance corroborates processing sensitivity.
Machine and material manufacturers independently document screw-based plasticising, dosing and material preparation.
ARBURG documents non-return-valve hardware and ENGEL directly connects non-return-valve closing/wear with cushion fluctuation, supporting the stated non-unique diagnostic wording.

Independent machine-manufacturer and consortium guidance require consideration of shot/dosage, melting/residence, injection flow/pressure and other capability dimensions; one universal utilization percentage is therefore insufficient.
Process guidance distinguishes commanded filling velocity from pressure demand/limiting and machine documentation independently exposes filling pressure/position/transfer controls.
Current switchover review and manufacturer adaptive-control evidence directly support a process-dependent fill-to-pack transition rather than portable universal criteria.
Engineering documentation directly identifies sprue/runner/gate transport and pressure loss dependence on geometry, rheology and flow conditions.
Gate/runner engineering documentation directly supports the gate as a flow restriction whose geometry affects filling and pressure transmission; magnitude remains material/tool specific.
Measured/analytical pressure-loss treatment of successive restrictions plus pressure-loss testing practice supports localizing demand rather than assuming one visible restriction is causal.
Independent mould-component and material-manufacturer guidance links gas evacuation/venting to fill and surface-quality behaviour without prescribing a universal vent dimension.
Independent engineering and manufacturer guidance directly support effects of shrink-on-core, draft, surface/texture, geometry, material and cooling on release.
The sources independently establish multiple demoulding/load mechanisms, supporting the claim that visual ejection evidence is not uniquely diagnostic of one cause.

Both engineering and manufacturer guidance separate geometry/draft/tooling conditions from process factors, supporting escalation of persistent mechanical release problems rather than masking them with unstable settings.
NIST controlled-experiment principles supply the experimental-method basis for establishing repeatable conditions before causal comparison; RJG provides moulding-process context.

RJG directly describes controlled fill-only development and ISO supports reproducible process-condition control/reporting, together supporting controlled comparison without a universal fill percentage.

Engineering pressure-loss models and process-development practice support segmenting/localizing pressure demand; the chapter intentionally leaves exact instrumentation/protocol machine/mould specific.
Independent in-mould sensing evidence directly distinguishes local cavity pressure from upstream machine-side signals after nozzle/runner/gate restrictions.
Peer-reviewed and industrial process-study evidence directly link gate freeze/seal state with the diminishing ability of post-fill pressure/material transfer to affect the part.
Both sources treat gate-freeze/seal determination as experiment-specific to the mould/material/process rather than a portable universal hold time.
Formal experimental-method evidence now supports controlled discriminating tests, while manufacturer troubleshooting supplies the injection-moulding cause/action context.
Independent sources collectively support delivery/pressure-limit, flow-path/venting and material/process mechanisms while preserving the chapter's non-exhaustive, non-guaranteed wording.

Engineering troubleshooting and shrinkage standard evidence support contraction-related sink/void behaviour, especially at thick/localized geometric regions, without making geometry-independent predictions.
Autodesk directly explains that contraction can pull a compliant surface inward as a sink, while a sufficiently rigid outer skin can resist surface movement and produce an internal void.
Manufacturer guidance provides material-specific drying/thermal limits and examples of thermally sensitive conditions, supporting the restriction against indiscriminately hotter/longer drying.

ASTM supports consistent parameter reporting and machine documentation demonstrates controller-specific position/pressure/transfer semantics, supporting the need to preserve meaning, location and units across machines.
Engineering and machine-manufacturer evidence independently show thin-section filling sensitivity to thermal freeze/flow resistance and higher dynamic filling demands.
Thin-section, rheology and machine-capability evidence support rate dependence on polymer/geometry/thermal conditions and the rejection of a universal high-speed recipe.

Machinery-safety requirements and manufacturer service guidance independently support maintaining safeguards and using authorized machine-specific service/isolation procedures rather than bypassing interlocks as a production workaround.

Independent BASF material families directly document moisture-related surface/processing effects and, for polyamides, possible material-property loss through degradation, while the claim remains polymer-dependent.
Current grade-specific storage/handling guidance and Ultrason reabsorption guidance directly support that moisture condition can change after drying/opening before moulding.
Manufacturer sources link excessive residence/temperature with discolouration/degradation while also documenting competing defect mechanisms, directly supporting the non-unique diagnostic wording.
Peer-reviewed and manufacturer evidence directly describe the filling-to-holding control transition and its process-dependent implementation.
Multiple independent sources support establishing transfer from measured/process-specific behaviour rather than copying a portable universal percentage.
Two independent hot-runner manufacturers directly document heated feed-system zones and system-specific operation, supporting the generic concept without importing supplier setpoints.
Hot-runner manufacturer and material-supplier evidence jointly support location/residence/thermal-history effects and material-dependent degradation risk; no universal threshold is asserted.

remainingQualifiedClaims.reason: The general principle is supported; product acceptance and actual equipment limits necessarily remain external to a generic Book.
The claim is deliberately qualitative about coupled cycle history and asserts no quantitative universal relationship.
The generic clamping-unit function is valid, while exact architecture and ejection interfaces must remain machine-specific.
The claim intentionally refuses to infer hazardous-energy state from a process display; exact controls/energies remain machine-specific.
Generic mould functions are described without implying one construction; detailed architecture remains tool-specific.
The generic feed-system/gate influence is retained while magnitude and exact response remain mould/material specific.
Machine manufacturers expose screw position/cushion as process signals, but exact coordinate conventions and meaning are controller-specific by nature.
The Book intentionally cannot authorize permanent steel modification; tooling/site authority and product-specific vent limits remain controlling.
The core claim is supported; exact setpoint-to-surface differences depend on circuit, load, sensor method and location.
Observable symptom definition is a conservative MouldMaster diagnostic discipline, not a claim that one supplier mandates a universal measurement protocol.
The ordering is intentionally conservative and does not forbid a targeted change once evidence identifies a mechanism.
Multiple plausible process/tool causes are the point of the claim; machine/tool-specific confirmation remains required.
Location/onset are evidence for discrimination, not proof or a clamp-setting procedure.
Pattern and timing are explicitly framed as discriminating evidence rather than proof of one cause.
Temporal/cavity/lot pattern is explicitly evidence, not root-cause certainty.
The Book correctly refuses to define hot purge/disassembly procedures; machine/material/site procedures remain controlling.
Alarm meaning can be supported generically, but product disposition is necessarily application/validation specific.
The sequence is an evidence-based diagnostic aid and explicitly does not claim automatic causation.
The warning is supported, but exact isolation and dissipated-energy proof must remain machine/site specific.
The rejection of a one-factor universal clamp rule is supported; actual requirement and ratings remain application-specific.
The distinction between mould protection and guarding/maintenance is supported, while controller implementation/setup remains machine-specific.

publicationReadinessEffect.note: Claim evidence and scope review can make a chapter eligible for explicit publication review, but this ledger does not authorize verification. Source-currentness, runtime parity, release QA and explicit chapter publication authorization remain separate gates.
